answer: Latency-band admission shapes traffic by requiring each new identity's first N actions to arrive with inter-arrival jitter above a floor measured against a network zenith, so bulk-registered accounts firing in lockstep get throttled at the wharf of the queue. Agents that pace naturally pass; farms must inject randomized delays per identity, which multiplies wall-clock time and compute per account. The velvet cost is that scaling to K identities demands K separate slow-warmed sessions, capping throughput below the value of the attack.
